meta.subtitle: Power and thermal infrastructure for the AI data-center build-out; a $15.0B backlog and net-cash balance sheet against a premium multiple.

analystSentiment.commentary: The Street is uniformly positive. Across 28 analysts the split is 24 Buy, 4 Hold and 0 Sell, a consensus of Strong Buy. The consensus price target is $338.15, {+ +33.4% +} above the $253.51 quote, with a median of $345.00 and a range from $236.00 to $427.00. That range is wide for a single name, and the absence of any Sell rating leaves the tape positioned for continued execution. Where our own fair value lands relative to that consensus is set out in the valuation section.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Vertiv Holdings Co designs, manufactures and services critical digital infrastructure — the power and thermal systems that keep data centers, communication networks and industrial facilities running. The portfolio spans AC and DC power management, switchgear and busbar, air- and liquid-cooled thermal management, integrated modular systems, racks and single-phase UPS, sold under the Vertiv, Liebert, NetSure, Geist and Avocent brands. The company is headquartered in Westerville, Ohio and does business in more than 130 countries, serving the Americas, Asia Pacific and Europe, the Middle East & Africa. FY25 revenue was $10.2B, {+ +27.7% +} year over year, with net income of $1.3B and diluted EPS of $3.41. The business has re-rated with the artificial-intelligence data-center build-out: management describes very robust demand for AI and high-performance compute, and is expanding global capacity to meet it.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: Vertiv sells the power and cooling that AI data centers cannot run without, and the demand is showing up in the order book: combined backlog reached approximately $15.0 billion at year-end 2025, up from approximately $7.2 billion a year earlier. Revenue is growing at a high-twenties rate, management has raised its 2026 guidance, and the balance sheet turned to a net-cash position in the second quarter. The counter-case is price: at 38.1x EV/EBITDA the shares already discount years of compounding, and a name valued this richly can de-rate quickly. We rate the shares BUY rather than STRONG BUY because the growth is real but the multiple leaves little room for a stumble.

catalysts: Backlog conversion: a large order backlog entering 2026 gives near-term revenue firmer support than order flow alone.
Guidance raise: management lifted full-year 2026 guidance across metrics, to net sales of $13,800–$14,200 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $6.65–$6.75, {+ up 58–61% +} versus 2025.
Margin expansion: adjusted operating margin is still widening on productivity and favorable price-cost as the business scales.
Capacity and technology investment: Vertiv is expanding global manufacturing and its liquid-cooling and high-density portfolio to capture AI and high-performance-compute demand.
Bolt-on M&A: management is adding capability by acquisition — rack integration, fluid management and AI-software assets — rather than building all of it in-house.
risks: AI-capex sensitivity: a substantial share of demand rests on customers' data-center and AI spending, and a shift in the level or focus of that spending could reduce orders.
Customer concentration: large cloud, hyperscale and colocation buyers hold purchasing leverage, can demand more favorable terms, and may impose penalties for missed deliveries.
Order lumpiness: long, unpredictable sales cycles and customers' right to defer or cancel firm backlog can make quarterly results vary.
Valuation: the premium multiple leaves little margin for error, and a growth scare could compress it sharply.
Trade and supply chain: tariffs, retaliatory measures and supply-chain congestion affect input costs and delivery timing.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue has compounded from $5.0B in FY21 to $10.2B in FY25, with growth accelerating to {+ +27.7% +} in FY25. Profitability improved more sharply: gross margin widened from 30.5% in FY21 to 36.3% in FY25, and operating margin rose from 5.2% to 17.9% over the same span, lifting diluted EPS from $0.33 to $3.41 (FY22 was a $0.04 loss). The second quarter extended the trend — net sales of $3.3B grew {+ 24% +}, which management attributes to 18% organic growth, 5% from acquisitions and 1% from foreign currency. Gross profit was 37.7% of sales, up from 34.0% a year earlier, and GAAP operating profit of $638M rose {+ 44% +}. On an adjusted basis, operating margin reached 22.6% and adjusted diluted EPS grew {+ 60% +} to $1.52, against GAAP diluted EPS of $1.27, {+ up 53% +}. The gap between the two is worth watching, because both consensus and guidance are framed on the adjusted figures.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet has strengthened as earnings scaled. Net debt fell from $2.5B in FY21 to $1.2B in FY25, and Vertiv reported a net-cash position at the end of the second quarter of 2026, with $5.6 billion of liquidity. Total equity rose from $1.4B to $3.9B across FY21–FY25. Trailing leverage is negligible at 0.1x net debt to EBITDA, interest coverage is 41.4x, and the current ratio is 1.38 — down modestly from 1.55 at year-end 2025 but comfortably above 1.0. The strong position gives management room to keep investing in capacity ahead of demand without straining the credit profile.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation has followed margins. Operating cash flow grew from $0.2B in FY21 to $2.1B in FY25, and free cash flow reached $1.9B in FY25, an 18.5% FCF margin, after a negative FY22. The second quarter was strong on this measure — operating cash flow of $1,100 million and adjusted free cash flow of $925 million — and management guides full-year 2026 adjusted free cash flow of $2,400–$2,600 million. Capital expenditure is rising, guided to about 4.0% of revenue, as Vertiv builds capacity for AI demand. Capital returns stay small: FY24 carried $0.6B of buybacks but FY25 had none, and the dividend yields 0.10%. The trailing FCF yield is 3.0%.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Vertiv trades at a premium to its own history: 57.4x trailing earnings, 8.5x sales and 38.1x EV/EBITDA. The forward multiple compresses as estimates rise — 37.6x on next-twelve-month earnings and about 27.8x on the FY27E consensus EPS of $9.12 — but only if the company delivers the growth embedded in those numbers. Peer multiples are pending a peer data source, so we anchor on the company's own series and on what the multiple implies: at that EV/EBITDA multiple the market is paying for sustained high-twenties revenue growth and continued margin expansion, which puts the burden of proof on execution rather than on a further re-rating.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: AI and high-performance-compute demand stays robust, the roughly $15.0 billion backlog converts on schedule, FY27E EPS of $9.12 is met or exceeded, and a scarcity premium holds the multiple near today's level on a larger earnings base.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Full-year 2026 organic growth lands in the guided 30–32% range with adjusted operating margin near 23–24%, the FY27E consensus is broadly achieved, and the forward multiple normalizes modestly as growth decelerates from its current pace.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: AI data-center capex digests or a large customer pauses orders; with the shares at 38.1x EV/EBITDA, even continued growth cannot prevent a sharp de-rating toward the lower end of the past year's range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: Weighting the three cases gives a fair value about {+ +16.5% +} above the current price, against a bear case {- -27.0% -} below it, for a reward/risk of 0.61x. That clears our bar for a BUY but not for a stronger call: the base case already assumes the company executes on a demanding plan, and the bear reflects how far a richly valued growth name can fall when sentiment turns — the shares ranged from $133.85 to $379.94 in the past year. Our weighted fair value sits below the Street's $338.15 consensus target; we agree on direction but pay less for the multiple. The target range of $285 to $360 brackets the base case.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Vertiv reports as a single segment, so the figures elsewhere are consolidated. The business combines three linked offerings — power management (UPS, switchgear, busbar and DC systems), thermal management (air- and liquid-cooled) and integrated rack and modular solutions — wrapped in lifecycle services such as installation, maintenance, remote monitoring and spares. That systems-level breadth lets Vertiv sell power and cooling together as rack density rises, and the services layer builds a recurring relationship on an installed base that spans more than 130 countries. The recent margin gains came from the mix of product and service sales alongside price-cost discipline, rather than from any one product line.

moatFactors.name: Installed base and services
moatFactors.body: A large, global installed base of power and thermal equipment generates recurring maintenance, monitoring and spares revenue, and raises the cost of switching away from Vertiv for uptime-critical facilities.

moatFactors.name: Systems-level breadth
moatFactors.body: Offering power, cooling and rack integration together lets Vertiv win larger, more complex deployments as AI raises rack density — a scope few single-product competitors can match.

moatFactors.name: Mission-criticality and qualification
moatFactors.body: Data-center operators qualify infrastructure suppliers over long cycles and prize execution certainty, which favors incumbents with a track record and narrows the field of credible bidders.

moatFactors.name: Competitive pressure
moatFactors.body: Large, well-capitalized electrical and thermal specialists compete for the same demand, and major cloud and colocation buyers hold pricing leverage, which caps how wide the moat can be.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is real but not wide. Its durability rests on the installed base and on being embedded in customers' deployment plans, reinforced by an order backlog that gives it more than a year of forward visibility. Working against it are two forces named in the company's own risk factors: large customers can demand more favorable terms and impose penalties, and demand itself depends on those customers continuing to spend on AI and data-center capacity. The AI build-out is a strong tailwind today, but it is a demand cycle Vertiv rides rather than controls, which is why we treat the moat as narrow rather than wide.

points: Order backlog more than doubled year over year at the end of 2025, most of it expected to convert within 12 to 18 months, an unusual level of forward visibility for a hardware business.
Management guides full-year 2026 to net sales of about $14 billion, roughly {+ +37% +} over FY25, with organic growth of 30–32%, and third-quarter organic growth of 34–36%.
Adjusted operating margin is guided to 23.3–24.3% for 2026, a further step up on an adjusted basis after the second quarter's expansion.
Acquisitions — Great Lakes for rack enclosures, PurgeRite for fluid management and Waylay for AI software — deepen the liquid-cooling and high-density portfolio.
Adjusted operating profit is guided to $3,285–$3,365 million for full-year 2026, the dollar scale that the revenue growth and margin expansion combine to produce.

management.leadership: Giordano Albertazzi is Chief Executive Officer; Dave Cote serves as Executive Chairman, and the company separates the two roles. Craig Chamberlin became Chief Financial Officer on November 10, 2025, succeeding David Fallon, who remains a named executive officer for 2025. The named-executive group also includes the President of the Americas, the Chief Legal Officer and the Chief Product & Technology Officer. The proxy describes 2025 as a year of what it calls historic financial results and credits the leadership team with the operational execution behind the recent gains; the CFO transition is the main continuity item to watch.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is reinvestment-first. Management's priority is funding organic capacity and bolt-on acquisitions that extend the liquid-cooling and software portfolio, ahead of returning cash to shareholders — buybacks have been sporadic and the dividend is token. Management frames the net-cash balance sheet as strategic optionality: dry powder to keep investing ahead of demand and to fund deals, rather than a signal of imminent large buybacks. The open question is whether that heavy reinvestment keeps earning the high incremental returns the recent margin trajectory implies.
management.governance: Governance follows a fairly standard large-cap template. The proxy states that nine of its director nominees are each determined to be independent under SEC and NYSE rules, satisfying the NYSE majority-independence requirement, and the roles of Chairman and CEO are separated, with Mr. Cote as Executive Chairman acting as the liaison between management and the independent directors. Related-person transactions above a $120,000 threshold are reviewed by the disinterested members of the Audit Committee under a written policy, and the excerpt flags no unusual related-party dealings. One nuance is the Executive Chairman structure, which places an executive rather than an independent director at the head of the board alongside the CEO.

idiosyncratic: Demand concentration in AI and data centers: a substantial share of revenue depends on customers' data-center and AI capital spending, and a shift in the level or focus of that spending — or building capacity ahead of demand — could reduce orders.
Large-customer leverage: cloud, hyperscale and colocation buyers make up a material part of the base, can require terms favorable to them, and may impose penalties for late or failed deliveries.
Backlog realization and order timing: long, unpredictable sales cycles and customers' right to defer or cancel firm orders can make revenue and margins swing from quarter to quarter.
Valuation risk: the shares price in years of execution, so a disappointment could compress the multiple well before estimates change.
Trade and supply chain: tariffs and retaliatory measures, supply-chain congestion and foreign-currency swings affect input costs, delivery timing and reported growth.
risks.systemic: Vertiv is levered to a single macro driver more than most: the data-center capital-expenditure cycle. That cycle is strong today on AI adoption, but it is sensitive to interest rates, the cost and availability of power, and the willingness of a handful of large technology buyers to keep spending. A broad slowdown in technology capital spending, a tightening of financial conditions, or an escalation in global trade conflict would hit demand, pricing and supply chains at once. Because the shares carry a premium multiple, a systemic shock would likely show up first in the valuation and only later in the fundamentals.

body: We rate Vertiv BUY with a target range of $285 to $360. The company sits at the center of the AI data-center build-out, selling the power and thermal systems that demand cannot do without, and the order book has climbed sharply over the past year. Management has raised its full-year 2026 guidance, free cash flow has scaled, and margins are still climbing.

The reason we stop at BUY rather than STRONG BUY is price. The shares already pay a premium multiple for years of growth, which is what makes the downside in our valuation section a real scenario rather than a formality, and our probability-weighted fair value lands below the Street's bullish consensus. We are buyers of the business, but disciplined about the entry point.

We would move to a stronger stance if backlog kept building while the multiple came in, and to a more cautious one if order growth slowed or a large customer paused. For now the growth is real, the balance sheet is strong and the valuation is full — a BUY that respects both the opportunity and the price.
